improvisational

/im-prov-uh-ZAY-shuh-nul/ · adjective

What It Means

Improvisational means done or created spontaneously, without prior preparation or planning.

The band's improvisational encore, invented entirely on the spot, became the most talked-about part of the concert.

Example

Halfway through the cooking competition, the judges removed every recipe card from the kitchen. The contestants had to invent dishes on the spot from whatever sat in the mystery pantry, tasting and adjusting as they went with no plan to follow. One chef combined ingredients she had never paired before and plated a dessert that had existed nowhere until that very moment. The judges praised her improvisational cooking as the boldest work of the night.

The chef created her dish spontaneously in the moment, without any prior preparation or plan, which is what improvisational means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

spontaneous: Spontaneous means done on impulse, without planning - a spontaneous road trip happens because the urge struck. Improvisational describes a way of working, often scheduled and skilled: an improvisational troupe plans to take the stage and then invents the material live. The impulse makes something spontaneous; the in-the-moment craft makes it improvisational.

extemporaneous: Extemporaneous means composed or performed on the spot, and it is the formal word for unscripted speaking - an extemporaneous toast or debate rebuttal. Improvisational reaches beyond speech into whole works of theater, music, and cooking invented live. An extemporaneous speaker finds words as she goes; an improvisational artist builds the entire piece as she goes.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

scripted: following a prepared written text

rehearsed: practiced repeatedly in advance

Where it sits · how little planning guides the work — unrehearsed → improvisational → haphazard

unrehearsed vs. improvisational: Unrehearsed only means something was not practiced beforehand, while improvisational means actively creating something new in the moment.

haphazard vs. improvisational: Improvisational work is unplanned but still skillful and purposeful, while haphazard work is unplanned and careless, with no guiding skill at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — im-

Prefix — im-: not

Prefix — pro-

Prefix — pro-: before, ahead

Root — vis

Root — vis: from Latin videre and visus, to see

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the act or process of

Suffix — -al

Suffix — -al: characteristic of, pertaining to

Put it together

Put it together: Improvisational goes back to Latin improvisus, 'not seen beforehand,' from im- (not) plus pro- (before) plus visus (seen). The suffix -ation names the act of creating what could not be foreseen, and the suffix -al, meaning 'characteristic of,' completes the adjective: characteristic of work invented in the moment, before anyone could see it coming.

Use the root in a new word: revise

Use the root in a new word: revise: Editors revise a manuscript by literally 'seeing it again,' using the same Latin root vis that hides inside improvisational.

Word Choice

neutral register, common in the arts

Improvisational most often describes performance and creative work (improvisational theater, an improvisational jazz solo, an improvisational style). It emphasizes skillful creation in the moment; for a quick makeshift object or repair, English usually prefers the shorter form improvised (an improvised shelter).
